# Daily Dashboard V0.5.11

Dashboard now checks for updates in native startup, independently of the web interface and display lock. On Windows, enable **Settings → Updates → Automatically download and install on startup** once to download and verify newer stable installers, install silently and restart Dashboard on later launches.

- Notifications are on by default. Automatic downloading and installation require opt-in; legacy automatic modes reset to notify, disabled checks remain disabled, and choices saved by this version persist.
- Temporary connection failures retry without blocking Dashboard. Missing assets or failed SHA-256 verification leave the current version running.
- Public releases work without an account. Optional private-repository authentication and saved tokens are retained while the repository is private.
- macOS supports checks/downloads and manual installation; Windows installation controls are omitted.
- Recovery launches and `--skip-update` bypass startup updates. Development builds skip them. A relaunch routed to an existing instance does not start another updater.
- Rollback pauses automatic installation so it is not immediately undone.
- Includes demo-only README screenshots, an in-app update notification and source privacy checks. Repository visibility and history are unchanged.

Install this release once to enable the new startup behaviour. This runs when Dashboard launches, including at Windows sign-in if Dashboard is already launched there; it does not register a Windows autostart entry. Product identity and settings location remain unchanged.

[Startup update guide](https://github.com/BananaAficionado/DailyDashboard/blob/main/docs/startup-updates.md).

## Verification

Frontend build/regressions, native policy/release/retry/checksum tests, Windows cross-compilation and updater browser contracts pass. Settings/layout checks cover the documented display/scaling configurations. Windows CI builds the installer and runs native tests. Actual Windows installation/restart and physical monitor transitions still require Windows hardware testing.
